target.title: feat: let plugins control inbound debounce policy
target.body:
Related: #54565

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins cannot currently decide whether rich inbound WhatsApp messages should bypass debounce or choose a debounce window for a specific account, DM, group, conversation, or sender. Doing either requires changing product defaults or adding more core configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a typed `inbound_debounce` plugin hook. The hook receives the channel's default action, duration, a read-only debounce key, conversation context, and media/location/quote facts. It may explicitly debounce, bypass, or select a duration.

WhatsApp now consults this hook while preserving its current defaults. Control commands still dispatch immediately. Rich batches preserve all media and structured context, and split safely when multiple quotes or locations cannot be represented without data loss.

This is an API-based alternative to the product-level approaches in #103049 and #100970. It lets plugins provide those policies without adding native product settings.

AI-assisted with Codex.

## User Impact

There is no behavior change when no plugin implements the hook. Plugins can opt media, locations, or quoted replies into batching and can choose different windows for DMs, groups, accounts, conversations, senders, or their own policy scopes.

The hook is bounded by a two-second timeout, preserves per-conversation arrival order, keeps control commands immediate, and cannot replace the debounce key to merge unrelated conversations.

## Evidence

- `pnpm build` passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts`: 67 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/hooks.inbound-debounce.test.ts`: 2 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/inbound-dispatch.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/monitor-inbox.streams-inbound-messages.test-support.ts`: 149 passed across the focused WhatsApp shards.
- Focused legacy-message E2E: 1 passed; the full file has two existing active-listener timing failures that reproduce on `origin/main`.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` passed with 10,652 public exports and no forbidden subpaths.
- Source/extension boundary checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh autoreview passed with no accepted or actionable findings.

Remote Testbox proof was unavailable because the Blacksmith CLI is not installed and the AWS Crabbox fallback has no credentials in this environment, so the repository's allowed local linked-worktree fallback was used.
